title: सकार गा.वि.स. वैतडीका प्राथमिक विद्यालयमा दलित विद्यार्थीहरूको अवस्था {Sakar ga.bi.sa. Baitadika prathamik bidyalayama dalit bidyarthiharuko abastha}
authors: भट्टराई, गोपाल दत्त Bhattrai, Gopal Dutt
nepali: नेपाल एक बहुजातीय, बहुभाषिक, बहुधार्मिक, र बहुसांस्कृतिक देश हो । नेपालका यिनै विविध जातीका विविध पक्षहरुमध्ये “सकार गा.वि.स. वैतडीका प्राथमिक विद्यालयमा दलित विद्यार्थीहरुको अवस्था” सम्बन्धी खोज गरिएको यो एक अध्ययन हो । यस अध्ययनमा  प्राथमिक विद्यालयमा दलित विद्यार्थीको भर्ना र उपस्थिति, कक्षा कोठा र विद्यालय क्रियाकलापमा सहभागिता, शिक्षक र गैरदलित विद्यार्थीले दलित विद्यार्थीप्रति गर्ने व्यवहार, दलित विद्यार्थीको विद्यालय सहभागितामा समस्या र  त्यसका कारणहरुजस्ता उद्देश्यमा आधारित भई अनुसन्धानकार्य गरिएको थियो । उक्त उद्देश्यहरूपूरा गर्नको लागि अध्ययनमा वर्णनात्मक अनुसन्धान ढाँचा प्रयोग गरिएको थियो । यस अध्ययनको लागि अध्ययन क्षेत्रभित्रका जम्मा पाँचओटा प्रा.वि.हरुलाई नमूनाको रुपमा लिइएको थियो । अध्ययनकार्यको लागि तथ्याङ्क संकलन गर्न विद्यार्थी भर्ना सम्बन्धी तथ्याङ्क संकलन फारम, उपस्थिति फारम, अवलोकन फारम, अन्तर्वार्ता तथा समूह छलफल निर्देशिकाको निर्माण एवम् प्रयोग गरी प्राथमिक तथा सहायक श्रोतका माध्यमबाट सूचना संकलन गरिएको थियो । अध्ययन क्षेत्रका प्रा.वि.मा गैर दलित विद्यार्थीको तुलनामा दलित विद्यार्थीको भर्ना कम पाइयो । दलित विद्यार्थीमा छात्र र गैर दलित विद्यार्थीमा छात्राको भर्नादर बढी रहेको पाइयो । विद्यालयमा गैर दलित विद्यार्थीको तुलनामा दलित विद्यार्थीको विद्यालय उपस्थिति कम पाइयो । त्यसैगरी कक्षाकोठामा गैरदलित विद्यार्थीको तुलनामा दलित विद्यार्थीले कक्षा कार्य र गृहकार्य कम मात्रले गर्ने, छलफलमा पनि कम सहभागी हुने, कक्षामा पछाडि बस्ने जस्ता क्रियाकलापहरू गरेको पाइयो । विद्यालयमा जातिगत रुपमा भने कुनै भेदभावको व्यवहार   पाइएन । शिक्षक र गैर दलित विद्यार्थीहरुले दलित विद्यार्थीहरुलाई कक्षा सिकाई र अतिरिक्त क्रियाकलापमा विभिन्न किसिमको सहयोग र उचित व्यवहार गरेको पाइयो । दलित विद्यार्थीहरूविद्यालयमा कम सहभागी हुनुमा गरिवीको कारण, विद्यालय पोशाक, भर्ना शुल्क, कपि, कलम किन्ने पैसाको अभाव, अन्य क्षेत्रजस्तो शिक्षाबाट तुरुन्त प्रतिफल प्राप्त नहुनु, दलित अभिभावकहरुको चेतनामा कमी, परीक्षामा अनुत्तीर्ण हुनु, लैङ्गिक विभेद, दलित महिलाहरूनिरक्षर हुनु, रुढीबादी धारणा, दलित स्वयम्ले आफूलाई तल्लो वर्गको ठान्नुजस्ता पक्षहरूप्राप्त भए । उल्लेखित समस्याहरूसमाधानको लागि दलित विद्यार्थीको पायक पर्ने ठाउँमा विद्यालय खोल्ने, विहानी कक्षाको व्यवस्था, विद्यालय पोशाक र छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान, निःशुल्क पाठ्यपुस्तक वितरण, घरदैलो जागरण कार्यक्रम, साक्षरता कार्यक्रम, लैङ्गिक समतासम्बन्धी तालिम, विद्यालयमा दलित शिक्षकको व्यवस्था तथा जनचेतना र सशक्तिकरण जस्ता कार्यक्रमहरूसम्बन्धित पक्षले संचालन गर्नुपर्ने देखिन्छ ।
american_english:
Nepal is a multi-caste, multi-lingual, multi-religious and multi-cultural country.
Among the various aspects of these diverse castes of Nepal, this is a study conducted on "The Status of Dalit Students in Primary Schools of Sakar VDC, Baitadi."
In this study, the research work was based on objectives such as enrollment and attendance of Dalit students in primary school, participation in classroom and school activities, the behavior of teachers and non-Dalit students toward Dalit students, and the problems and causes in the school participation of Dalit students.
To fulfill those objectives, a descriptive research design was used in the study.
For this study, a total of five primary schools within the study area were taken as the sample.
For the study, to collect data, student enrollment data collection forms, attendance forms, observation forms, and interview and group discussion guides were developed and used, and information was collected through primary and secondary sources.
In the primary schools of the study area, Dalit students' enrollment was found to be lower than that of non-Dalit students.
It was found that the enrollment rate of boys among Dalit students and of girls among non-Dalit students was higher.
At school, Dalit students' attendance was found to be lower than that of non-Dalit students.
Likewise, in the classroom, compared to non-Dalit students, Dalit students were found to do class work and homework only to a small extent, to take less part in discussion, to sit at the back of the class, and to engage in such activities.
At school, no behavior of caste-based discrimination was found.
Teachers and non-Dalit students were found to give various kinds of support and proper treatment to Dalit students in classroom learning and extra activities.
The factors found behind Dalit students' lower participation in school were poverty, school uniform, admission fees, lack of money to buy notebooks and pens, not getting an immediate return from education as in other fields, low awareness among Dalit parents, failing examinations, gender discrimination, Dalit women being illiterate, orthodox attitudes, and Dalit people themselves considering themselves lower class.
To solve the problems mentioned, it appears that the concerned parties should run programs such as opening schools in places within easy reach of Dalit students, arranging morning classes, providing school uniforms and scholarships, distributing free textbooks, door-to-door awareness programs, literacy programs, training on gender equality, arranging Dalit teachers in schools, and public awareness and empowerment.
british_english:
Nepal is a multi-caste, multi-lingual, multi-religious and multi-cultural country.
Among the various aspects of these diverse castes of Nepal, this is a study undertaken on 'The Condition of Dalit Pupils in the Primary Schools of Sakar VDC, Baitadi'.
In this study, the research work was grounded in objectives such as the enrolment and attendance of Dalit pupils in primary school, participation in the classroom and in school activities, the conduct of teachers and non-Dalit pupils towards Dalit pupils, and the problems and their causes in the school participation of Dalit pupils.
In order to fulfil those objectives, a descriptive research design was employed in the study.
For this study, a total of five primary schools within the study area were taken as the sample.
For the study, in order to collect data, forms for the collection of pupil enrolment data, attendance forms, observation forms, and interview and group discussion schedules were devised and used, and information was gathered through primary and secondary sources.
In the primary schools of the study area, the enrolment of Dalit pupils was found to be lower than that of non-Dalit pupils.
It was found that the enrolment rate was higher for boys among Dalit pupils and for girls among non-Dalit pupils.
At school, the attendance of Dalit pupils was found to be lower than that of non-Dalit pupils.
Likewise, in the classroom, in comparison with non-Dalit pupils, Dalit pupils were found to do class work and homework only to a small extent, to take a smaller part in discussion, to sit at the back of the class, and to engage in such activities.
At school, no behaviour of caste-based discrimination was found.
Teachers and non-Dalit pupils were found to offer various kinds of support and proper treatment to Dalit pupils in classroom learning and extra-curricular activities.
In the lower participation of Dalit pupils in school, the factors found were poverty, school uniform, admission fees, lack of money to buy exercise books and pens, not obtaining an immediate return from education as in other fields, a lack of awareness among Dalit parents, failing examinations, gender discrimination, Dalit women being illiterate, orthodox attitudes, and Dalit people themselves regarding themselves as of a lower class.
For the solution of the problems mentioned, it appears that the parties concerned ought to conduct programmes such as opening schools in places within easy reach of Dalit pupils, arranging morning classes, providing school uniform and scholarships, distributing free textbooks, door-to-door awareness programmes, literacy programmes, training relating to gender equality, arranging Dalit teachers in schools, and public awareness and empowerment.
australian_english:
Nepal's a multi-caste, multi-lingual, multi-religious and multi-cultural country.
Out of all the different sides of Nepal's castes, this study looks at "The Situation of Dalit Students in Primary Schools in Sakar VDC, Baitadi."
The research work was built around objectives like Dalit students' enrolment and attendance at primary school, their participation in the classroom and school activities, how teachers and non-Dalit students behave towards Dalit students, and the problems and causes around Dalit students' school participation.
To meet those objectives, the study used a descriptive research design.
For this study, five primary schools in the study area were taken as the sample.
To gather data, the study developed and used student enrolment data forms, attendance forms, observation forms, and interview and group discussion guides, collecting information from primary and secondary sources.
In the study area's primary schools, Dalit students' enrolment came out lower than non-Dalit students'.
The enrolment rate came out higher for boys among Dalit students and for girls among non-Dalit students.
At school, Dalit students' attendance came out lower than non-Dalit students'.
In the classroom too, Dalit students were found doing less class work and homework than non-Dalit students, taking less part in discussions, sitting down the back of the class, and doing things like that.
At school, no caste-based discrimination was found.
Teachers and non-Dalit students were found giving Dalit students all sorts of support and fair treatment in classroom learning and extra activities.
The things behind Dalit students taking less part in school came out as poverty, school uniform, admission fees, not having money for notebooks and pens, not seeing an immediate payoff from education like in other areas, low awareness among Dalit parents, failing exams, gender discrimination, Dalit women being illiterate, old-fashioned attitudes, and Dalit people themselves seeing themselves as lower class.
To sort out the problems mentioned, it looks like the relevant parties should run programmes like opening schools within easy reach of Dalit students, setting up morning classes, providing school uniforms and scholarships, handing out free textbooks, door-to-door awareness programmes, literacy programmes, gender equality training, putting Dalit teachers in schools, and public awareness and empowerment.
